extracted.intended_audience: NIDDK extramural researchers, grant applicants, NIH/NIDDK program staff, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: An official NIDDK report describing the Institute's guiding principles, funding policies, portfolio metrics, and trends (FY2014–FY2023) used to inform funding decisions and evaluate performance across mechanisms, investigators, clinical research, and training. Intended to guide applicants and internal programmatic review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a Vigorous Investigator-Initiated Research Portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: One of NIDDK’s core values: prioritize and sustain investigator-initiated research (RPGs, especially R01 awards) as a central component of the portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes ~70% of NIDDK’s research portfolio is focused on RPGs (especially R01s). NIDDK regularly reviews its research portfolio and makes strategic adjustments based on scientific and programmatic balance considerations. Actions supporting this value include establishing and maintaining healthy R01 paylines, shifting funding among activity codes (e.g., from R37 and P01 to R01s), and increasing paylines for established investigators and ESIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Pivotal Clinical Studies and Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: A core value requiring substantial support for human subjects research and clinical trials across appropriate mechanisms (R01, U01, K23, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK tracks human subjects research and clinical trial projects and spending (e.g., more than 17,600 human subjects awards and >$8.4B invested FY2014–FY2023; >5,000 clinical trial awards and >$2.8B invested). The Institute leverages grants and cooperative agreements and follows NIH definitions for human subjects research and clinical trials to identify and report portfolio composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote a Steady and Diverse Pool of Talented New Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: A core value focused on supporting Early Stage Investigators (ESIs), New Investigators (NIs), and diversity among applicants/awardees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies include differential (more generous) paylines for ESIs (ESI payline increased to the 25th percentile in FY2020 and maintained), monitoring numbers of ESI applications and awards, and tracking age and demographic trends (mean/median PI age, racial/ethnic success rates). NIDDK notes efforts to enhance workforce inclusion where persistent gaps exist (e.g., fewer applications and awards for PIs identifying as Black or African-American).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster Exceptional Research Training and Mentoring Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: A core value to support trainees across F, K, and T mechanisms and to evolve mechanisms as needed to support training objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK monitors counts and spending for Fellowship (F), Career Development (K), and Training (T/TL1) awards (e.g., ~$1.3B awarded to trainees FY2014–FY2023). The Institute documents trends (increases in F31, decreases in F32 and some T32 activity) and pilots alternate mechanisms (TL1) to meet training needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure Knowledge Dissemination through Outreach and Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: A stated core value to disseminate research findings via outreach and communications (listed among the five guiding principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This report focuses primarily on the first four core values, but includes this principle as part of overarching mission/vision guiding NIDDK activities and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria for Charts and Tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit rules about which data are included in the figures and analyses: most charts exclude initiative (RFA) data and the Special Statutory Type 1 Diabetes Program funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for Figures 1, 2, 9, & 10 (which include initiative data), the data in all charts exclude initiatives (i.e., Requests for Applications, or RFAs). The data presented do not include grants funded through the Special Statutory Funding Program for Type 1 Diabetes Research unless otherwise noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and Categorization of Funding Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK categorizes portfolio activity by funding mechanism/activity code (RPGs, SBIR/STTR, Research Centers, Research Careers, Training, Other Research, Contracts/IAAs) and uses these categories to assess portfolio composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report lists example activity codes for each mechanism (e.g., R01, R21, U01, P01 for RPGs; R41-R44 for SBIR/STTR; P20/P30/P50 for centers; all K awards for Research Careers; F/T for Training; R13/R18/R24 etc. for Other Research). Figures track the percentage/funding by mechanism across FY2014–FY2023 to inform strategic adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory SBIR/STTR Allocation Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR allocation is congressionally mandated to be 3.65% of the annual extramural allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK treats the SBIR/STTR allocation as a fixed, statutory portion of the extramural budget when analyzing and planning the portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Peer Review Scoring System and Translation to Percentiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewer-assigned numeric impact scores (1–9; lower is better) with percentile rankings for most R01s; applications in the lower half may be streamlined and unscored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most R01 applications receive percentile rank scores based on impact scores; streamlined applications do not receive numeric scores and are 'unscored.' For more detail, the report points to NIH Grants & Funding- Peer Review: Scoring. NIDDK uses percentile scores as a key piece of information to inform funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: R01 Payline Policy and Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK establishes and publishes R01 paylines by fiscal year for five classes: general (<$500K), >$500K, New Investigator, Early Stage Investigator (ESI), and ESI First Competitive Renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 documents paylines FY2011–FY2023. NIDDK strives to maintain healthy R01 paylines and notes the ESI payline was increased by 7 points to the 25th percentile in FY2020 and maintained thereafter. Paylines are used as a guide but the institute also exercises programmatic discretion to skip some grants within the payline and to support programmatically important applications beyond the general payline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Payline and Programmatic Discretion Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement of how closely funding decisions follow paylines and the extent of discretionary funding beyond paylines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report examples: NIDDK funded 99% (n=405) of all grants (excluding ESI) that received a percentile score of 1–16 and funded 5% (n=43) of R01 applications (excluding ESI) that scored beyond the 16th percentile. For ESIs, NIDDK funded 95% (n=82) of ESI applications scoring 1–25 and funded 4% (n=7) beyond the 25th percentile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring New vs Renewal R01 Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Track counts and proportions of new R01 applications versus renewal applications to assess submission and renewal dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From FY2014 to FY2023, new R01 applications increased (2,007 to 2,523; +26%) while renewal applications decreased (430 to 334; -22%), with renewals falling from 18% to 12% of all R01 applications—indicating a shift toward submitting new applications rather than renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: R01 Portfolio Cost and Inflation Adjustment Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track total R01 spending (direct+indirect), mean and median R01 costs, and adjust for inflation using BRDPI for trend interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominal R01 spending rose from $739M to $1.2B (FY2014–FY2023; +63% nominal; +~29% after BRDPI inflation adjustment). Mean total cost of R01 rose from ~$375K to ~$493K (31% increase). Use BRDPI to correct for inflation (FY2014 base) when interpreting trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-PI (MPI) R01 Monitoring and Team Science Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Track the number/proportion of multi-PI R01s to assess growth of team science approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-PI R01s increased from 11% of the R01 portfolio in FY2014 to 27% in FY2023. NIDDK recognizes multi-PI grants as an opportunity for team science on complex problems and monitors this trend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Identification of Human Subjects Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NIH definition to identify awards involving human subjects: intervention/interaction with living individuals or use of identifiable private information/biospecimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants were identified using the NIH human subjects definition. NIDDK reports a 28% increase in number of human subjects awards and 35% increase in spending across FY2014–FY2023; R01s constitute ~50% of the human subjects research portfolio in FY2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Definition and Stewardship Policy Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH definition of clinical trial: prospective assignment to interventions to evaluate effects on health-related outcomes; stewardship reforms (2016 onward) require clinical trials to be submitted via clinical-trial-specific FOAs (effective due dates on/after Jan 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK reports an 83% increase in clinical trial project count and 75% increase in spending FY2014–FY2023. The report notes the policy change improved clinical trial categorization and reporting and likely contributed to observed portfolio growth in clinical trial counts and spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Stage Investigator (ESI) Definition and Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI defined per NIH: completed terminal degree or end of postgraduate clinical training within past 10 years and not previously competed successfully for a substantial NIH independent research award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK established differential ESIs paylines starting FY2012; ESI payline was raised to the 25th percentile in FY2020 and maintained. NIDDK tracks ESI application and award counts (e.g., ESI awards rose substantially after payline increase) and notes that once an ESI/NI receives their first competing award they are reclassified as established investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring Investigator Age and Career-Stage Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track mean and median ages of funded R01 PIs and counts of PIs by career stage (Established, New, ESI) to inform workforce planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK reports changes in mean/median ages (e.g., mean/median stabilized or decreased FY2020–FY2022 then increased in FY2023) and monitors counts of PIs by career stage. ESIs and NIs are counted only in the year they receive their competing award and not in subsequent years of their award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring Racial/Ethnic Diversity and Success Rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and report self-identified race data for R01 applicant and awardee PIs to measure diversity and identify gaps in success rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 reports counts and success rates by race (e.g., White PIs: 6,672 applicants, 3,111 awarded, 47% success; Black/African-American: 248 applicants, 78 awarded, 31% success). NIDDK and NIH initiatives (e.g., COSWD, UNITE) are cited as efforts to address disparities. Note: NIH redacts data where sample size <11 for privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Portfolio Metrics and Mechanism Evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Track counts and spending for Fellowship (F), Career Development (K), and Training (T/TL1) awards and adapt mechanisms to meet training needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From FY2014–FY2023 NIDDK awarded >$1.3B for trainees; observed trends include a 477% increase in F31 awards, decreases in F32 awards, relative stability in K99 counts. NIDDK piloted TL1 (first awards in FY2021) as an alternate to T32 for one division; TL1 counts and trainee numbers are tracked in Table 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy/Redaction Policy for Small Sample Sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policy requires redaction of data where sample size is less than 11 to protect privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables in the report use redaction (e.g., '** = actual value <11') and the report explicitly states this privacy protection standard when presenting demographic breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio Review and Strategic Adjustment Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK practice of regularly reviewing the research portfolio and making strategic adjustments based on scientific and programmatic balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report states NIDDK 'regularly reviews its research portfolio and makes strategic adjustments as needed based on scientific and programmatic balance considerations' and documents how funding shifts (e.g., from some activity codes to others) and policy changes (paylines, stewardship) have been applied.
